neighbours.label: the verb of a player's turn-taking action in a game (takes a shot, gave up runs)
fire: After the foul, the guard takes two free throws.
In golf, the player farthest from the hole takes the next shot.
The starter gave up four hits in the second inning.
If the kick misses, the other team takes possession.
The goalkeeper takes a short run before the penalty.
Their closer gave up a home run in the ninth.
When the bell rings, each player takes one card.
The bowler takes a wicket with his first ball.
quiet: After the foul, the guard stood at the line.
In golf, the player farthest from the hole is away.
The starter pitched well in the second inning.
If the kick misses, the crowd groans loudly.
The goalkeeper stands still before the penalty.
Their closer struggled badly in the ninth.
When the bell rings, each player sits down.
The bowler looks tired after his first over.

notes: Weak pole (max 5.7), no dominant token. Probe: 'the shooter takes a second one' fired 0.43, but 'gave up three runs' only 0.05. Best guess from the top example; likely to fail.
